sentences.text: The FIR is lodged by the Applicant Rajesh Pandey.
He has stated that he was a Director and CEO of Telemachus High- tech Pvt. Ltd.
One Shantibhai Chheda and Firdoz Contractor were the investors in that company.
In 2007-2008, he got in contact with one Saket Shrivastav of Lucknow.
He introduced the informant/Applicant to the Respondent No.1 Saurabh Mishra.
Both of them represented to the Applicant/informant that they were the contractors and they were in a position to get contracts for the informant.

During further meeting, they told the informant that one project behind Lucknow Airport was to come up and that both of them would help the informant in getting that contract; but for that, the informant had to pay Rs.1  to 2 Crores.
Similarly, in 2016 they represented to the informant that they could get a contract for the transport of 3/6 25-APPLN-ST-14856-23.odt around 25,000 Metric Ton of sand.
The accused extracted money in the name of Rashtroday Prakashan Pvt. Ltd. on some pretext.
After the first meeting with the Respondent No.1, the informant had gone to his house to meet him again at Lucknow.
That meeting was attended by Respondent No.1's wife Smita and his daughter.
The informant had paid Rs.50 lakhs to him in the presence of his wife and her daughter.
The FIR further mentions that certain amount was transferred in the account of News Times Post International.
In short, the FIR mentions that the Respondent No.1 obtained Rs.13.20 crores on various pretext and returned only Rs.1.20 crores.
Thus the Respondent No.1 and the other accused had misappropriated this huge amount.

4. The Respondent No.1 was arrested on 30/05/2023 and he was granted bail by the Additional Sessions Judge, Thane, vide his order dated 24/07/2023, after considering allegations against him as mentioned in the FIR.
Learned Judge observed that after arrest, during the police custody, the police had sufficient opportunity to interrogate the accused.
The Applicant 4/6 25-APPLN-ST-14856-23.odt was arrested on 30/05/2023.
At the time of passing of the order he was in custody for one month and 25 days.
Therefore, the learned Judge had taken into consideration the necessity of custodial interrogation and had observed that sufficient opportunity was given to the investigating agency.
More importantly, learned Judge had observed that the medical papers of the Respondent No.1 show that he was a diabetic patient.
After he was sent to jail, he had sustained leg injury.
The Respondent No.1 was admitted in J.J. Hospital.
Treatment could not be given there.
Thereafter, he was admitted to S. L. Raheja Hospital, Mumbai.
The medical papers show that the right leg below the knee of the Respondent No.1 was amputated on 17/07/2023 and treatment for another leg was going on.
There was complications in his health.
Looking at the health condition of the Respondent No.1, the learned Judge was inclined to grant bail to him.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the informant submitted that the entire allegations in the FIR are directed mainly against the 5/6 25-APPLN-ST-14856-23.odt Respondent No.1.
He is benefited to a huge amount.
There are allegations that he had forged work order purportedly issued by a government authority.
For that purpose his custodial interrogation was necessary.
6. Learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 supported the impugned order and the reasons mentioned in that order.
7. I have considered these submissions and I do not find fault with the reasons given by the Additional Sessions Judge in granting bail to the Respondent No.1.
As noted by him, the investigating agency had sufficient opportunity to interrogate the Respondent No.1.
More importantly, the learned Judge has given sufficient reasons with reference to the health condition of the Respondent No.1.
This was the main consideration apart from the merits of the case.
8. Considering that the impugned order is a well reasoned order, the Respondent No.1's further custody, by cancelling bail 6/6 25-APPLN-ST-14856-23.odt granted in his favour, is not justified.
There is no point in keeping him in custody during the entire period of trial.
There are no allegations of breach of conditions or misuse of liberty.
With the result, the application is rejected.

(SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.)
